UADataType.Description: Used to model a simple key-value-pair for the application defined extension of the FLAMES specification with additional information that must be identified by its name.
Used to identify a specific carrier instance throughout a production system uniquely.

Field.Name: TypeId
Field.Description: Identification for a certain type of carrier.

Field.Name: UniqueId
Field.Description: Identification of a specific carrier instance.

UADataType.Description: Used to identify a position on a facility component, on a transport pallet, or on a carrier throughout a procudtion system uniquely.

Field.Name: OwnerClass
Field.Description: The kind of object to the position belongs to.

Field.Name: PositionId
Field.Description: Unique identification of the position system wide, or on its owner depending on the OwnerClass.

Field.Name: OwnerTypeId
Field.Description: Identification of the position owner’s type.

Field.Name: OwnerId
Field.Description: Unique identification of the position owner’s specific instance.

UADataType.Description: Used as the data type for the ToolIdentifierType variable type and other applications that require unique identification of a tool.

Field.Name: Name
Field.Description: The name of a tool. Tools with equal names are tools of the same kind, and with the same basic geometry and technology values etc.

Field.Name: Duplonumber
Field.Description: The duplonumber of the tool. It is used to distinguish tools with the same name.

Field.Name: UniqueId
Field.Description: A tool may be equipped with a chip on its holder, or have another feature that identifies a tool uniquely with a single value.

UADataType.Description: Used to identify a specific transport pallet instance throughout a production system uniquely.

Field.Name: TypeId
Field.Description: Identification for a certain type of transport pallet.

Field.Name: UniqueId
Field.Description: Identification of a specific transport pallet instance.

UADataType.Description: Used as the value of an ApplicationDataEntry. Its value is limited to common simple data types.
Used to identify an object to be transported uniquely.

Field.Name: Tool
Field.Description: The transport object is a tool with this identifier.

Field.Name: Workpiece
Field.Description: The transport object is a workpiece with this identifier.

Field.Name: Carrier
Field.Description: The transport object is a carrier with this identifier.

Field.Name: TransportPallet
Field.Description: The transport object is a transport pallet with this identifier.

UADataType.Description: Used as identifier for a workpiece in the scope of a production control system.

Field.Name: PartTypeId
Field.Description: The identification of the part type / operation plan of the workpiece.

Field.Name: ProductionOrderId
Field.Description: The identification of a certain production order, i.e. a certain amount of workpieces of a special part type to be produced.

Field.Name: SerialNumber
Field.Description: The serial number of the explicit workpiece within the scope of the production order.

Field.Name: UniqueId
Field.Description: An application defined unique identification number or name for the workpiece.

UAVariableType.Description: Used to identify a fixed system position of facility component uniquely.

UAVariable.Description: When a facility component has multiple available positions with the same UniqueId (from the viewpoint of a production control system), the position that is currently in use may be indicated with this optional variable.

When a facility component has multiple available positions with the same UniqueId (from the viewpoint of a production control system), the identification can be extended by specifying this additional variable.
The duplonumber of the tool. It is used to distinguish tools with the same name.
The name of a tool. Tools with equal names are tools of the same ind, and with the same basic geometry and technology values etc.
A tool may be equipped with a chip on its holder, or have another feature that identifies a tool uniquely with a single value.

UAVariableType.Description: Used to describe a span of a tool's life without an absolute reference for the minimum or maximum values etc.

UAVariable.Description: The unit in which a tool's life is measured.
Additional indicator for the semantics of the EngineeringUnits.

UAVariableType.Description: Used to store information about the absolute life of a tool and optional meta information.

UAVariable.Description: Describes how the tool life is consumed. Up-counting tool life means, a new tool has the value 0 and its value increases until NominalAmount. Down-counting means, a new tool has the value of NominalAmount and its value decreases until 0.

Describes the total amount of tool life that a new tool has. Whether the life is counting up or down is irrelevant for this variable's value, i.e. also up-counting tool life shall have a nominal value > 0. Up-counting tool life must instantiate this variable for a client to be able to determine the remaining amount.
The value, when reached, indicates that the tool shall be changed soon. Whether the life is counting up or down must be taken into account, when determining whether the warning limit is reached.

UAObjectType.Description: Used for requesting and supplying extended data needed for the operation of the facility component with a production control system.

UAMethod.Description: Used to supply handling information for a certain part or carrier type.

uax:Description.uax:Text: Used to differentiate the parameter's value in order of its expected layout.
Refers to a certain carrier or part type the parameters belong to.
This contains a set of bytes that define parameters describing carrier or part types regarding e.g. dimensions, weight, ranges for allowed pressures etc.

UAMethod.Description: Used to supply the coordinates for a certain facility component's position.

uax:Description.uax:Text: Identification of the position the coordinates belong to.
Translatory offset in X, Y, and Z axis of the position relative to the position on the base object. The unit of the offset is [μm] (or [1/1000 mm]).
Rotatory offset in A, B, and C axis of the position relative to the position on the base object. The unit of the offset is [1/1000 °].

UAMethod.Description: Used to supply information for a certain workpiece on a facility component's position.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The location hierarchy of the workpiece (ordered bottom up). May be needed to identify the workpiece on the facility component.
Identification properties of the workpiece.
This contains a set of bytes that define parameters describing the workpiece regarding e.g. material, state, etc. Information from the workpiece argument may be included in this argument, too.

UAObjectType.Description: Holds differentiated state information for a production control system.

UAVariable.Description: Represents the operational state of the facility component compliant with the states defined in VDI 3423.
Indicates if the facility component can participate in automatic system operation or not.
Indicates whether the facility component requires service intervention by an operator.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated when a OPC UA sub-component of an AutomationStateType instance changes its value.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
Represents the operational state of the facility component compliant with the states defined in VDI 3423.
Indicates if the facility component can participate in automatic system operation or not.
Indicates whether the facility component requires service intervention by an operator.

UAObjectType.Description: Represents an alarm that occurs on the machine tool.

UAVariable.Description: Vendor specific ID of the error. The value shall always be > 0.
The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.

This variable shall be sent, if the alarm text is stored in a production control system to override the Message property, which is used as the alarm text as default. When the variable is present, it must contain parameters that are replaced with placeholders of the message text stored in a production control system, or an empty array, if the message has no placeholders.

UAMethod.Description: The Confirm method defined in OPC UA Part 9 is changed to mandatory. When a condition of this type or its subtypes is confirmed by the client, the comment argument indicates whether the client has processed the request successfully, or not. An empty comment indicates the successful treatment of the condition. A numeric error code as comment indicates a failure. The comment error code can have special values that apply in the context of the respective condition. The comment error code 0 indicates an unspecified failure that occurred on the treatment of the condition.

UAVariable.Description: The ConfirmedState defined in OPC UA Part 9 is changed to mandatory.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generatedto signal a tool in the current NC program that is not in the magazine and should be fed directly from outside into the spindle, or to remove a previously fed tool.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
The name as it is used in an NC program of any tool of that specific type that shall be loaded into the spindle. An empty value means the same as if the variable was not present.
Holds the unique identification of of the tool that shall be removed from the spindle.
The duplonumber of the tool. It is used to distinguish tools with the same name.
The name of a tool. Tools with equal names are tools of the same ind, and with the same basic geometry and technology values etc.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated to signal the need for additional parameters for the handling of carriers or workpieces.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
The identifier of a specific "instance".
The location hierarchy of the carrier or workpiece (ordered bottom up), the parameters are requested for.
This is used to differentiate the object kind whose handling parameters are required.
This refers to a certain carrier or part type, the parameters are required for.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated to signal the need for the coordinates of a position within the scope of a production control system.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
The identification of the position the coordinates are requested for.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated to signal the need for a tool dataset that is not yet in a facility component's tool memory, or the dataset must be updated.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
The duplonumber of the tool whose dataset is needed. A value < 1 means the same as if the variable was not present.
The name of the tool whose dataset is needed as it is used in an NC program. An empty value means the same as if the variable was not present.
The holder ID of the tool whose dataset is needed. An empty value means the same as if the variable was not present.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated to signal the need for extended workpiece information for the handling of workpieces.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
The best-know location hierarchy of the workpiece (ordered bottom up), the information is requested for,

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated during a program run (if supported) to append this file to a production control system's data of the workpiece

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
The NodeId of a FileType instance with the measurement results to be retransferred.
Location hierarchy of the workpiece in machining (ordered bottom up) as additional information for identifying the workpiece.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated for the purpose of manually identifying objects on input/output positions on loading/unloading carriers or tools to or from the automated area.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
The position is occupied with an object, or not.

When the Occupied carriable is false, this variable shall not be present, or empty. In special cases, this variable may be empty, if an object exists on the position (Occupied = true), but the identification cannot be determined (e.g. code cannot be read).
Unique identification of the facility component position within the production system.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated when an activity that may lead to the deletion of a tool dataset was requested at the server.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
This enables the unique identification of a tool throughout a production system.
The duplonumber of the tool. It is used to distinguish tools with the same name.
The name of a tool. Tools with equal names are tools of the same ind, and with the same basic geometry and technology values etc.
Indicates if the tool is locked, e.g. because it is broken.
The variable contains the complete specific tool dataset with geometry and technology values as it is required to handle the tool.
The detailed image of a tool's life. When the tool's life is not managed at all, this shall not be send.
The unit in which a tool's life is measured.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated during a program run (if supported) to reintegrate the zero offsets into a production control system's data of the specific position on a workpiece carrie.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
Location hierarchy of the workpiece in machining (ordered bottom up) as additional information for identifying the workpiece.
The NodeId of a FileType instance with the zero offsets to be retransferred.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated when the controller reboots, or after a longer period of local operation or interrupted connectivity.
This event shall be generated, when a FacilityComponentPositionType instance has an Occupied variable and a sensor triggers a change of the position's occupation.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
The sensor's signal interpretation.
Unique identification of the facility component position within the production system.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated to inform a production control system about executed operations considering one or several workpieces' progress.

UAVariable.Description: Describes the type of operation executed and the consequences in a production control system.
The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
Unique identification of the facility component position within the production system.
Indicates whether parts will be scrap after the operation is executed, and the number of parts to report as scrap.

UAObjectType.Description: The event type serves as a base type for tool related events.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
This enables the unique identification of a tool throughout a production system.
The duplonumber of the tool. It is used to distinguish tools with the same name.
The name of a tool. Tools with equal names are tools of the same ind, and with the same basic geometry and technology values etc.

UAObjectType.Description: This is used to report an update of a tool's dataset. This can e.g. be a tool that was just used in an NC program, or whose dataset was updated by an operator.

UAVariable.Description: Indicates if the tool is locked, e.g. because it is broken.
The variable contains the complete specific tool dataset with geometry and technology values as it is required to handle the tool.
The detailed image of a tool's life. When the tool's life is not managed at all, this shall not be send.
The unit in which a tool's life is measured.
Describes the origin of the event. This may be used by a client to filter events that were e.g. triggered by itself.

UAObjectType.Description: This is used to report a tool dataset that was created.
This is used to report a tool dataset that was deleted.

This event type shall be generated to report the rearrangement of a tool in the tool storage of a facility component. This can e.g. be a tool that was interchanged between magazine and spindle. Another reasons may be the rearrangement of a tool inside the storage.

UAVariable.Description: The identification of the ToolPositionType to which the tool was stored. This variable may not be present, if there is no destination position or it is unknown (e.g. because the tool was taken from this position to outside a facility component in an unloading operation). For rearrangements this variable must be present.

The identification of the ToolPositionType from which the tool was removed. This variable may not be present, if there is no source position or it is unknown (e.g. because the tool was put to this position from outside a facility component in a loading operation).

UAObjectType.Description: This is used to report a completed loading operation of a tool to a facility component's storage.

UAVariable.Description: The identification of the ToolPositionType to which the tool was stored. This variable may not be present, if there is no destination position or it is unknown (e.g. because the tool was taken from this position to outside a facility component in an unloading operation). For rearrangements this variable must be present.
Describes the origin of the tool. This may be used by a client to filter events that were e.g. triggered by activities of a production control system.

UAObjectType.Description: This is used to report a completed unloading operation of a tool from a facility component's storage.

UAVariable.Description: The identification of the ToolPositionType from which the tool was removed. This variable may not be present, if there is no source position or it is unknown (e.g. because the tool was put to this position from outside a facility component in a loading operation).
Describes the destination of the tool. This may be used by a client to filter events that were e.g. triggered by activities of a production control system.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated to report a completed usage of a tool within an NC program.

UAVariable.Description: The amount of tool life consumed within the use. The value is unsigned, so whether a tool's life is managed counting-up or counting-down does not matter. The absolute value shall be given.
The unit in which a tool's life is measured.
The relative duration measured from the beginning of the NC program when the tool use began.

UAObjectType.Description: This is sent for every change in the components, or the state of the OccupancyReconciliationType.

UAVariable.Description: This indicates a certain failure a production control system must evaluate. It must only be sent, if the reconciliation was cancelled!

UAObjectType.Description: This is sent for every change in the components, or the state of the ProductionProgramType.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.

The program path and name. This is basically equal to the browse path from the facility component's FileSystem object as root to the FileType instance of the production program. If the facility component does not expose a FileSystem, this shall be the production program's name. The server shall use slashes (/) or backslashes (\) as path separator.
An arbitrary comment that can be provided for additional information on the last/current state of the program.
The last/current block of the program that was/is active.
The name of the last/current tool that was/is used in the program.

This value can be available after the regular end of the program giving a hint on the result of a measuring operation. This variable shall only be send, if the State is "Ended". This may e.g. be used by measuring machines to indicate the part quality.

When a program was aborted, an additional reason for the abortion can be given. Predefined reasons will lead to special reactions in the automatic production process. This variable shall only be send, if the State is "Aborted".

UAObjectType.Description: This is sent for every change in the components, or the state of the TransportUnitType.

UAVariable.Description: This shall be send, if a facility component's transport unit is a simple pallet exchanger. If the current position is undefined (e.g. because the transport device is moving) this property shall not be sent, too.
This indicates a certain failure a production control system must evaluate. It must only be sent, if the transport was cancelled!
The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance that caused the event, i.e., the facility component that executes the transport.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated for each executed movement of the generic transport. They shall not be generated for simple pallet exchange transports!

UAVariable.Description: The destination location hierarchy of the transport step (ordered bottom up).
The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance that caused the event, i.e., the facility component that executes the transport.
The source location hierarchy of the transport step (ordered bottom up)
The kind of transport that was executed in this transport step.
The kind of object that was transported in this transport step.

UAObjectType.Description: This event type shall be generated when a facility component reads the workpiece identification (e.g. as 2D code on a workpiece) during a transport and reports it to a production control system.

UAVariable.Description: The UniqueId of the FacilityComponentType instance the event refers to.
Unique identification of the facility component position within the production system.
Identification number as read from the workpiece.

UAObjectType.Description: Contains all subordinate facility components of a ControllingFacilityComponentType instance.

UAObject.Description: For each subordinate facility component, an instance of the FacilityComponentType must be contained in this list.

UAVariable.Description: Unique identification of the facility component within a production system.

UAObjectType.Description: Contains fixed system positions of a facility component that are relevant for the operation of a production control system.

UAObject.Description: For each system position, an instance of the FacilityComponenPositiontType must be contained in this list.

UAVariable.Description: Unique identification of the facility component position within the production system.

UAObjectType.Description: Describes a fixed position in the scope of a production control system. This can e.g. be the machining position of a machine tool, a fix position of a handling system, but also a position of an exchangeable gripper. For positions that are not fixed physically (gripper, pallet exchanger, etc.), a production control system regards these positions as fixed because it has no knowledge of grippers or similar.

UAVariable.Description: This must be instantiated, if the position has an occupations sensor. The facility component that owns the position must also generate events of the OccupancyStateChangedEventType.
Unique identification of the facility component position within the production system.

UAObjectType.Description: Represents a position of a facility component that can store a physical tool. This can e.g. be the spindle, or a position in a magazine.

UAVariable.Description: Reference to the tool within the ToolDataManagementType instance of a facility component that is currently stored on the position. If the position is empty, the value of this variable shall be Null.

UAObjectType.Description: Aggregates a wide range of versatile functionality. An instance of this type can be used to model arbitrary machinet tools, handling systems, clamping stations, I/O stations, passive storages, etc.

UAObject.Description: When extended data of the production control system is required by the facility component, this must be instantiated.

The automation state must be instantiated for all non-passive facility components like machine tools, handling systems, clamping and I/O stations etc. Purely passive facility components like storage racks that are only accessible vie the production system do not need an automation state.

UAVariable.Description: Represents the operational state of the facility component compliant with the states defined in VDI 3423.
Indicates if the facility component can participate in automatic system operation or not.

UAObject.Description: This must be instantiated, if the facility component supports any functionality requiring file transfers.
This must be instantiated (as an addition to the ToolDataManagement and ToolStorage), if the facility component supports the direct tool supply via spindle.

UAMethod.Description: When a tool was supplied/removed by an operator or a handling device, the facility component shall be informed by calling this method.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The ID of the tool that was loaded into the spindle, or an empty value if no tool was loaded.
The ID of the tool that was unloaded from the spindle, or an empty value if no tool was unloaded.

UAObject.Description: The production management must be instantiated if the facility component supports the execution of NC programs.
Holds information about the current selected NC program.

UAVariable.Description: The program path and name. This is basically equal to the browse path from the facility component's FileSystem object as root to the FileType instance of the production program. If the facility component does not expose a FileSystem, this shall be the production program's name. The server shall use slashes (/) or backslashes (\) as path separator.

UAObject.Description: Shows in which of the possible states, defined by the ProductionStateMachineType, the program is currently in and generates respective events at state transitions.

UAMethod.Description: Used to start the execution of an NC program that is used in production. It is not intended for starting utility programs that might exist for arbitrary tasks.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The program path and name that should be started. This is basically equal to the browse path from the facility component's FileSystem object as root to the FileType instance of the program to be started. If the facility component does not expose a FileSystem, this argument shall be the name of the program to be started. The server shall accept slashes (/) and backslashes (\) as path separator.
Location hierarchy of the workpiece to be machined (ordered bottom up). This is provided as additional information for identifying the workpiece to be machined.

Indicator if automatic start is released. When this is false, the facility component can pause before actually executing the program. This might be necessary, when an operator must confirm the machining because it is e.g. a new program.

When the program could be started as requested, this shall be Null. When the execution of a program cannot be started for logical reasons, the method call shall succeed but this argument shall have a non-Null numerical value. That means, if this argument is not Null, the ProductionProgram must not be started/changed!

UAMethod.Description: Used to inform the facility component about a changed mode of the automated environment. The set mode can influence the decisions of the facility component in case of disruptions of the automated processes.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The automation mode, the facility component is supposed to regard in operation.

UAObject.Description: This must be instantiated, if the facility component supports the management of tool data, which usually applies for machine tools.

UAMethod.Description: Used to transfer a tool dataset into the facility component’s tool memory. If the tool dataset is already existing, it shall be updated. Otherwise, a new dataset shall be created.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The ID of the tool's existing or new dataset.
The complete specific tool dataset with geometry and technology values as it is required to handle the tool. This can for example be an xml string or any other format as ByteString.

UAObject.Description: This must be instantiated, if the facility component supports the management of tools, which usually applies for machine tools.
When the facility component is able to execute transports, this must be instantiated. This can apply to handling systems, as well as e.g. machine tools with pallet exchangers, or else.

UAMethod.Description: Used to request the execution of a generic or an exchange transport.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The kind of transport to be executed.
The kind of object to be transported. The value of this variable must match the sourceObject and destinationObject arguments.
The source location hierarchy of the transport (ordered bottom up).
The object to be transported.
The destination location hierarchy of the transport (ordered bottom up).
Only for exchange transports, a destination object may be given.

When the transport could be started as requested, this shall be Null. When the execution of a transport cannot be started for logical reasons, the method call shall succeed but this argument shall have a non-Null numerical value. That means, if this argument is not Null, the TransportUnit must not be started/changed!

UAObject.Description: The state of the transport unit's current transport is represented by this component.

UAVariable.Description: Unique identification of the facility component within a production system.

UAObjectType.Description: The ControllingFacilityComponentType is the entry point for a FLAMES OPC UA server. I.e., there must be exactly one instance of this type organized by the Objects folder of the OPC UA server. A controlling facility component is itself a facility component and may be the controller of further subordinate facility components.

UAObject.Description: This list of subordinate controlled facility components must only be instantiated, if the ControllingFacilityComponentType instance is the controller of further components like clamping stations, I/O stations, simple machines (washing machine, measuring machine, …) etc.
This object must be instantiated if at least one position of this or a subordinate facility component supports the occupancy reconciliation.

UAObject.Description: The state of the current reconciliation procedure.

UAObjectType.Description: Used to support direct tool loading and unloading e.g. to or from the spindle of a machine tool.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The ID of the tool that was loaded into the spindle, or an empty value if no tool was loaded.
The ID of the tool that was unloaded from the spindle, or an empty value if no tool was unloaded.

UAObjectType.Description: Aggregates components to be used, if at least one position of this or a subordinate facility component supports the occupancy reconciliation.

UAMethod.Description: Used to request the complete occupancy reconciliation.

uax:Description.uax:Text: When the reconciliation could be started as requested, this shall be Null. When the execution of a reconsiliation cannot be started for logical reasons, the method call shall succeed but this argument shall have a non-Null numerical value. That means, if this argument is not Null, the OccupancyReconciliation must not be started/changed!

If the facility component does not expose a FileSystem, this shall be the production program's name. The server shall use slashes (/) or backslashes (\) as path separator.

UAObjectType.Description: The state machine for the OccupancyReconciliationType.

UAObject.Description: The active state. For each relevant position, an Event of type PendingOccupancyReconciliationConditionType is generated and must be processed by the client.
This transition marks the state change from the Active to the Active state. This can be necessary when components or properties of the OccupancyReconciliationType change within the Active state.
The transition from the Active state to the Cancelled state. The occupancy reconciliation was aborted.
The transition from the Active state to the Finished state. The occupancy reconciliation has been executed successfully.
This state signalizes a failed occupancy reconciliation (already for a single relevant position).
This transition marks the state change from the Cancelled to the Idle state. It indicates a reset after an aborted occupancy reconciliation.
This state signalizes that the occupancy reconciliation has been executed successfully.
This transition marks the state change from the Finished to the Idle state. It indicates a reset after a successfully executed occupancy reconciliation.
Inactive state of the occupancy reconciliation.
The transition from the Idle to the Active state. The reconciliation request was accepted and is now execution.

UAObjectType.Description: The state machine for the ProductionProgramType.

UAObject.Description: This state signalizes, the production program run has been terminated but without being finished completely as planned. Function M30/M02 was not executed.
This transition marks the state change from the Aborted to the Initialized state. It indicates the program has been reset after aborting, or another program was initialized.
This state signalizes that the production program has been ended in the planned way executing the M30/M02 function.
This transition marks the state change from the Ended to the Initialized state. It indicates the program has been reset to initial state after its regular end, or another program was initialized.
Initial state of production program. Program is not running.
The transition between the Initialized and Aborted state. The production program is being aborted without having started (not a meaningful transition).
The transition from the Initialized to the Running state. The production program is being started.
The interrupted state. The production program is not currently running.

The transition from the Interrupted state to the Aborted state. The production has been interrupted and is now being terminated but without being finished completely as planned. Function M30/M02 was not executed.
The transition from the Interrupted state to the Running state. The production program has been interrupted and is restarted from the point before the interruption.
The running state. Production program is running.

The transition from the Running state to the Aborted state. The production has been running and is now being terminated but without being finished completely as planned. Function M30/M02 was not executed.
The transition from the Running state to the Ended state. The production has been running and has been ended in the planned way executing the M30/M02 function.
The transition from the Running state to the Interrupted state. The production has been running and is now interrupted (program is halted e.g. by M0 function but still active).

The transition from the Running state to the Running state. This transition may be necessary to report changes of the optional components of the ProductionProgramType (e.g. LastProgramBlock) that occur in the running NC program by generating an event of the ProductionProgramTransitionEventType.

UAObjectType.Description: The state machine for the for the TransportUnitType.

UAObject.Description: The active state. The transport device is probably moving. When the transport is active, Events of type TransportStepFinishedEventType can be generated.
This transition marks the state change from the Active to the Active state. This can be necessary when components or properties of the TransportUnitType change within the Active state.
The transition from the Active state to the Cancelled state. The transport was aborted without successfully executing after having started.
The transition from the Active state to the Finished state. The transport has been executed successfully. An Event of type TransportStepFinishedEventType shall be send.
This state signalizes, the transport device failed to execute a requested transport.
This transition marks the state change from the Cancelled to the Idle state. It indicates the transport device has been reset after an aborted transport.
This state signalizes that a transport has been executed successfully.
This transition marks the state change from the Finished to the Idle state. It indicates the transport device has been reset after a successfully executed transport.
Inactive state of the transport device.
The transition from the Idle to the Preparing state. The transport request was accepted and is now preparing the actual execution of the transport.
The facility component is preparing for the actual transport. This can e.g. include waiting for additional information like handling parameters.
The transition from the Preparing to the Active state. The facility component has finished the preparation and is now executing the transport.
The transition from the Preparing to the Cancelled state. The facility component could not successfully prepare for the execution of the transport.
This transition marks the state change from the Preparing to the Preparing state. This can be necessary when components or properties of the TransportUnitType change within the Preparing state.

UAObjectType.Description: Contains components for the management and supervision of tool datasets held by a facility component.

UAObject.Description: For each tool dataset in the facility component's tool memory, an instance of the ToolType must be contained in this list. Which tools are present is a runtime information that will be changing in operation.

UAVariable.Description: Enables the unique identification of a tool throughout a production system.
The duplonumber of the tool. It is used to distinguish tools with the same name.
The name of a tool. Tools with equal names are tools of the same ind, and with the same basic geometry and technology values etc.
Indicates if the tool is locked, e.g. because it is broken.

UAVariable.Description: Contains the complete specific tool dataset with geometry and technology values as it is required to handle the tool. This can for example be an xml string or any other format as ByteString.
Meta information that can be used by the tool organization of a production control system. All tools with the unload marker set must be unloaded by an operator or automatically.
Identifies the version of the node if BaseModelChangeEvent is used. Refer to UAPart3 for the usage of the NodeVersion along with ModelChangeEvents.

UAMethod.Description: Used to transfer a tool dataset into the facility component’s tool memory. If the tool dataset is already existing, it shall be updated. Otherwise, a new dataset shall be created.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The ID of the tool's existing or new dataset.
The complete specific tool dataset with geometry and technology values as it is required to handle the tool. This can for example be an xml string or any other format as ByteString.

UAObjectType.Description: Contains all physical tool storage positions allowing a supervision of a facility component's tool stock. Even if a component has multiple tool magazines, all of their positions shall be kept in this one list.

UAObject.Description: For each tool position of a facility component that can store a physical tool, an instance of the ToolPositiontType must be contained in this list. This can e.g. be the spindle of a machine tool, a position in a magazine, or any other position representing a location of a physical tool on the facility component that is not necessarily accessible by an automated production system.

UAVariable.Description: Reference to the tool within the ToolDataManagementType instance of a facility component that is currently stored on the position. If the position is empty, the value of this variable shall be Null.
Unique identification of the facility component position within the production system.

This must be instantiated when a detailed image of a tool's life is required for the operation of a production system - which is usually the case, if tool management is supported. When a tool's life is not managed at all, this shall not be instantiated (e.g. measuring probes).
The unit in which a tool's life is measured.
Meta information that can be used by the tool organization of a production control system. All tools with the unload marker set must be unloaded by an operator or automatically.

UAObjectType.Description: Contains components for the request and supervision of transport execution.

UAVariable.Description: This shall only be instantiated, if the facility component's transport unit is a simple pallet exchanger.

UAMethod.Description: Used to request the execution of a generic or an exchange transport.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The kind of transport to be executed.
The kind of object to be transported. The value of this variable must match the sourceObject and destinationObject arguments.
The source location hierarchy of the transport (ordered bottom up).
The object to be transported.
The destination location hierarchy of the transport (ordered bottom up).
Only for exchange transports, a destination object may be given.

When the transport could be started as requested, this shall be Null. When the execution of a transport cannot be started for logical reasons, the method call shall succeed but this argument shall have a non-Null numerical value. That means, if this argument is not Null, the TransportUnit must not be started/changed!

UAObject.Description: The state of the transport unit's current transport is represented by this component.
